RESULT — PCA on the forms-of-capital variables (100-year slices, capital.csv), PC1 characterization of the Middle Neolithic (MN, 3400–3000 BCE) and Younger Neolithic (SG, 2900–2300 BCE).

METHOD (executed): PCA on the 12 Z-capital variables across the 39 hundred-year slices of capital.csv, correlation-matrix basis (each column centered and scaled to unit variance). PC1 scores computed per slice; phases assigned by BCE range (verified to match the file's group column: MN=3400–3000, SG=2900–2300). No missing values; both target ranges fully covered.

KEY NUMBERS
- PC1 eigenvalue = 43.67 (Kaiser form), explained variance ratio = 30.3%; PC1+PC2 ≈ 49.8% of total variance.
- PC1 loadings (drivers, sign arbitrary): strongest negative on ZCU_AU (copper/gold) −0.407, Zkeverz (pottery decoration) −0.382, ZHort (depot) −0.340, ZAxtSchwert (hatchets/swords) −0.299, ZDolch (daggers) −0.266; strongest positive on ZKeform (pottery form) +0.353, ZBeil (axes/celts) +0.242, Zamber +0.239. So PC1 is a composite "capital" contrast axis.

(a) PER-SLICE PC1
- MN: 3400 +0.591, 3300 +1.297, 3200 +1.780, 3100 +1.486, 3000 +1.806
- SG: 2900 +1.524, 2800 +1.620, 2700 +0.692, 2600 +1.131, 2500 +1.230, 2400 +1.310, 2300 +0.417

(b) MEAN ± SD PER PHASE
- MN: mean +1.392 ± 0.495 (min +0.591, max +1.806; n=5)
- SG: mean +1.132 ± 0.435 (min +0.417, max +1.620; n=7)

(c) WITHIN-PHASE TREND (per 100-yr, forward in time)
- MN: +0.262 per 100 yr → RISING through the phase (peaks ~3000–3200 BCE).
- SG: −0.121 per 100 yr → gradually DECLINING toward 2300 BCE.

(d) RELATIVE MAGNITUDE
- Overall series: mean 0.000 (by construction), SD 1.933, range −4.506 to +2.002.
- Group means: EN +1.765, MN +1.392, SG +1.132, LN −0.335, OBA −3.133, YBA −1.870.
- MN − SG (mean difference) = +0.260.
- Percentiles within the full series: MN ~46–85th (rising), SG ~44–72nd.
- Both phases sit on the POSITIVE side of the trajectory, well above the overall mean (0) and clearly above the later Late Neolithic / Old & Younger Bronze Age phases, which are negative.

(e) HYPOTHESIS (natural-language answer to the question)
In a PCA on the 12 forms-of-capital Z-variables analyzed in 100-year slices, PC1 explains ~30% of the variance. Both the Middle Neolithic (3400–3000 BCE) and the Younger Neolithic (2900–2300 BCE) are characterized by POSITIVE, ELEVATED PC1 scores — i.e., high composite forms of capital relative to the overall series (mean ≈ 0) and markedly higher than the subsequent Late Neolithic and Bronze Age phases (which turn negative). The two Neolithic phases differ mainly in level and direction: the Middle Neolithic is on average slightly higher (mean PC1 ≈ +1.4) and shows a rising trend through the phase (peaking around 3000–3200 BCE), whereas the Younger Neolithic is slightly lower (mean ≈ +1.1) and shows a gradual decline toward 2300 BCE. Thus the Middle and Younger Neolithic both occupy the high-capital (positive PC1) part of the trajectory, with the Middle Neolithic marginally higher and rising and the Younger Neolithic marginally lower and declining — marking the beginning of the long capital decrease that accelerates after 2300 BCE into the Late Neolithic and Bronze Age.

LIMITATIONS: (1) The data contain 12 Z-columns, not 11 as the prompt stated — all 12 were included. (2) PC1 sign is arbitrary (eigenvector convention); only relative magnitude/trajectory is interpretable. (3) Small per-phase samples (MN n=5, SG n=7) → trends are indicative, not statistically robust. (4) PCA basis (correlation vs covariance) changes PC1 negligibly (r≈0.997).

payload.workflow: Parsed capital.csv (comma decimals), kept all 12 Z-capital variables, treated the 39 rows as 100-year slices. Standardized each column (center+scale) and ran correlation-matrix PCA via eigen-decomposition (numpy; sklearn unavailable). Computed PC1 score per slice, assigned MN (3400–3000) and SG (2900–2300) by BCE (verified vs group column), and summarized per-slice values, mean±SD, within-phase linear slope, and relative magnitude vs the overall series and adjacent phases. Saved script and CSV tables as artifacts.
